title: Trump's FBI, DOJ 'know all the names', Epstein victim's ghostwriter says - NewsBreak
text:
By Knewz Staff ,
9 hours ago Virginia Giuffre’s memoir ghostwriter claims she knows the names on predator Jeffrey Epstein’s client list — and says top Washington officials do, too, Knewz.com can report.
Amy Wallace made an appearance on NewsNatio n to promote the book, Nobody’s Girl: A Memoir of Surviving Abuse and Fighting for Justice , and revealed she has hours of interviews with the late Giuffre, who detailed the years of abuse she suffered as the financier trafficked her to his rich and powerful friends.
Giuffre died in April, leaving Wallace to complete Giuffre’s memoir.
Ghostwriter knows ‘all the names’ Ghostwriter Amy Wallace confirmed her knowledge of the Epstein list — and who else is aware of the names on it — during an appearance on Ashley Banfield’s NewsNation show. By: @ NewsNation/YouTube “I know all the names … that are there, but every different scene, [Giuffre] had to make a decision about whether or not she was going to rename or name these people,” Wallace explained to Ashley Banfield.
“The book is the result of those decisions that she made,” the writer added.
FBI and DOJ ‘know the names’ In her book, co-authored by Amy Wallace, Virginia Giuffre revealed new details about claims she was trafficked to high-profile men including the British former prince Andrew Mountbatten Windsor, who’s denied any wrongdoing. By: @ NewsNation/YouTube Wallace stressed that U.S. government officials are also aware of the names Giuffre shared.
“Yes, I know who the names are. Virginia knows who the names are, but so does the FBI and so does the Department of Justice. That’s why there’s such a clamoring right now for the Epstein files to be released,” the ghostwriter said.
“It’s not just Virginia who’s come forward. It’s many, many brave women who came forward and talked to investigators,” she added.
Giuffre’s tapes are ‘safe’ Virginia Giuffre died at 41 at her home in Australia in April. By: MEGA “It exists in the FBI files. It exists in the Epstein files, as we now call them. She had named many names [in] depositions already that have been made public,” Wallace said of Giuffre. “There are four different document dumps, and there are many, many names in those.”
“They have the names, and they’ve had them for more than a decade,” the writer explained.
Wallace said she is very “aware someone could steal” the tapes from her interviews with Giuffre, though she assured Banfield that they are “safe.”
She then issued a bold warning: “Nobody can find them, so don’t break into my house. No one will be able to find them,” Wallace insisted.
‘Epstein list’ controversy President Donald Trump has called growing interest in the Epstein list a “Democrat hoax” despite campaigning on a promise that he would release the files. By: MEGA Epstein’s former friend Donald Trump promised he would release the names if elected to a second term as president.
After taking office in January, Attorney General Pam Bondi claimed she had the Epstein files “sitting on my desk.”
Bondi’s Justice Department did an about-face in July, saying Epstein never maintained a “client list” and that “no further disclosure would be appropriate or warranted.”
The DOJ claimed most of the material had been sealed by a court to protect Epstein’s victims, and even if the predator had gone to trial, “only a fraction” of it “would have been aired publicly.”
Epstein died in his New York City jail cell in 2019 while awaiting trial on trafficking charges.
Trump called the purported list the “Jeffrey Epstein Hoax” after getting blowback about the Justice Department’s decision.
Over the summer, Epstein co-conspirator Ghislaine Maxwell told Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche — one of Trump’s former personal lawyers — that “the president was never inappropriate with anybody. In the times that I was with him, he was a gentleman in all respects.” She also claimed he and Epstein were friendly but not “close friends.”
